holidays.name: National Repeat Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace doing things again. Replay the song you love, rewatch your favorite movie, or tell that great joke one more time. Nobody can say you're being repetitive when you're celebrating.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular fixture on quirky-holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: Psychologists call it the mere-exposure effect. People often like songs, images, and even jokes more the more often they encounter them, so a day of repeats has some science behind it.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Macaroons Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the chewy, coconut-packed chocolate macaroon. It's a sweet excuse to bake a batch or pick up a few from a bakery. Dipping the bottoms in melted chocolate is encouraged.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. Dessert fans have kept it going each June.
holidays.funFact: Coconut macaroons are not the same as French macarons. The name comes from the Italian word for paste, and the two cookies share ancestry but are very different treats. Coconut macaroons are naturally gluten-free.

holidays.name: National Egg Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the humble egg, whether scrambled, poached, deviled, or baked into a cake. Eggs are one of the most versatile foods in the kitchen, so there are plenty of ways to celebrate.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It is a favorite of breakfast lovers and egg enthusiasts.
holidays.funFact: A chef's toque is said to have one fold for each way a chef can cook an egg. The popular legend is that a hat with 100 folds marks a true master.
